say: Learn these four tests by heart. First, the task repeats. It happens many times a week, not twice a year.

panel.heading: Is this task a good candidate?
items: It repeats many times a week
It follows clear rules: when X happens, do Y
The data is already digital
Mistakes cost something

say: Second, it follows clear rules. You can write it as, when X happens, do Y. If the rule is, it depends on how I feel, it is not ready.

panel.heading: Is this task a good candidate?
items: It repeats many times a week
It follows clear rules: when X happens, do Y
The data is already digital
Mistakes cost something

say: Third, the data is already digital, in a form, a spreadsheet or an email. Paper records must be typed first, and Zapier or Make cannot do that typing for you.

panel.heading: Is this task a good candidate?
items: It repeats many times a week
It follows clear rules: when X happens, do Y
The data is already digital
Mistakes cost something

say: Fourth, mistakes cost something. A missed follow-up loses a sale.
Judgement calls, like refunds or angry complaints, stay with a person. Automation only gathers the facts and alerts her.

say: Ask the person who does the work to log one normal week: task, how often, minutes each time, apps involved, and what goes wrong.
Do not rely on memory. People forget the small, boring tasks, and those are often the best ones to automate.

say: Here is a worked example. Funmi runs a catering business in Ibadan, and her assistant logged one week.
Copying 25 orders at 3 minutes each took 75 minutes. Sending 25 confirmation emails at 2 minutes each took 50 minutes.

say: Zapier and Make think the same way. A trigger is the event that starts the automation, such as a new form response. Each automation has one trigger.

items: Trigger: the event that starts it
Filter checks the rule
Action uses mapped fields
Run saved in history

say: A filter checks a rule and stops runs that should not continue.

say: Then an action does the work, like sending an email. In it you map fields. You do not type a name into the email. You insert the Name field, so each run uses its own name.

say: Every run is saved in history to check later.

say: Typing a fixed value where a field should go is the most common beginner mistake. Every customer then gets the same name or amount.

panel.rule: Map fields from the trigger. Never type fixed values.

say: Zapier counts tasks. A task is any successful action. Triggers, filters and Formatter steps do not use tasks. The free plan gives 100 tasks a month, at the time of writing.
Make counts credits. Each module run is one credit by default, including every time a scheduled trigger checks for new data, even on quiet days.
The free plan gives 1,000 credits. So the schedule you choose changes the bill.
To remember. Good tasks repeat, follow clear rules, start digital, and cost something when done wrong. A one-week log beats memory. Weekly minutes times 4, divided by 60, gives rough monthly hours.
Map fields, never fixed values. And check the official pricing page on the day you quote.
